## Fatal findings

1. `cor-generalised-eigenspace-decomposition-for-a-split-minimal-polynomial` — Statement, `[L2]`, and proof step 1.1 ([item](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/cor-generalised-eigenspace-decomposition-for-a-split-minimal-polynomial.md:28)).

   The Statement and Given omit finite-dimensionality, while `[L2]` and step 1.1 apply `thm-primary-decomposition-for-an-endomorphism`. That dependency explicitly begins:

   > “Let \(T:V\to V\) be an endomorphism of a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) …”

   ([dependency](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-primary-decomposition-for-an-endomorphism.md:26)). Moreover, the library’s minimal-polynomial definition itself is scoped to finite-dimensional spaces ([definition](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-annihilator-ideal-and-minimal-polynomial-of-an-endomorphism.md:28)). Thus `[L2]` drops a load-bearing hypothesis and step 1.1 invokes the theorem outside its stated domain. The result can be generalized to algebraic infinite-dimensional operators by a different direct argument, but that argument is not supplied.

   Severity: **fatal** — missing hypothesis and inaccurate dependency restatement.

2. `ex-nilpotent-shift-and-its-single-primary-component` — title ([item](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/ex-nilpotent-shift-and-its-single-primary-component.md:4)).

   The unqualified title says the shift has “one primary component,” but the Example expressly includes \(n=0\) and correctly states that its primary decomposition is empty. Here \(\mu_T=1\), so there are no irreducible-power factors and hence zero primary components. The title is false on a boundary case admitted by the item itself.

   Severity: **fatal** — false title.
